text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The office of Russian prosecutor general has appealed to the government to postpone the auction of 38 percent stake of the Norilsk Nickel mining group.

- The Federal Security Service will investigate the origin of the money spent on the purchase of Russia's biggest telecoms company, Svyazinvest. A report on the results is expected in a month, says the paper.
- President Boris Yeltsin will make public the details of his meeting with Russia's chief banker Sergei Dubinin. The paper suggests that a form of monetary reform may be announced.
- Russian pianist Svyatoslav Richter, one of the greatest musicians of the 20th century, died in Moscow on Thursday.
SEVODNYA
- Russia's national power company Unified Energy System gives Western and domestic banks two weeks to submit bids to manage its issue of about $1 billion in convertible bonds.

- Russia's banking community is intrigued with the rumours about the misterious dissapearence of Andrei Gloriozov, a top official of Unikombank, which has been involved in a scandal around misuse of the federal budget money.
- Moscow administration will buy guns and ammunition illegally owend by the population, offering, for example, 834,900 roubles ($144) for assualt guns or 417,450 ($70) for a mine or a grenade.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA

- Russian banking business seems to be plunged into politics, says the paper in a reference to a wave of scandals involving some Russia's leading financial tycoons. This will leave Russia at the end of the world rating list, putting away western investers, warns the daily.
IZVESTIA
- Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko has turned to the language of ultimatums in a bitter row with Moscow over the fate of Russian TV correspondents arrested in Minsk.
- Construction workers in the Moscow underground have suspended work over dwindling financing.

- Russian peace-keeping forces stationed between Georgia and its separatist-minded republic of Abkhazia seem to be in no hurry to pack their bags despite the end of the term under the agreement keeping them there.
- The murder in St Petersburg of two top managers of the North-West shipping agency suggests the company is about to start turning hefty profits.
- Moldova will cater for the Russian army.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- Russian leaders should themselves explain their policies to TV viewers rather than leave it to overzealous, scandal-happy presenters.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- The Svyazinvest auction scandal heralds a new era in Russian politics where the interests of the state may prevail over corporate selfishness and unashamed plundering of state coffers.

- A investigation into the deeds of the Natsionalny Reservny Bank Chairman Alexander Lebedev is just one more proof that Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais no longer considers bankers who financed President Boris Yeltsin's election campaign as a cast of untouchables.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
